title: Find Indices of Stable Mountains
summary: Given an integer array height where height[i] represents the height of the i-th mountain, and an integer threshold, identify and return the indices of all mountains that are stable.
statement: Given an integer array height where height[i] represents the height of the i-th mountain, and an integer threshold, identify and return the indices of all mountains that are stable. A mountain is considered stable if the mountain immediately before it (if it exists) has a height strictly greater than the threshold. Note that the first mountain (index 0) is not stable.
constraints: A mountain at index i is stable when the immediately previous mountain’s height exceeds threshold.
Only indices one through n-1 can qualify.
Return all stable indices in increasing order.
reference_solution:
def stable_mountain_indices(height,threshold):
    return [i for i in range(1,len(height)) if height[i-1]>threshold]
hints: Eligibility depends solely on the immediately preceding height.
Enumerate candidate indices from one onward.
Append i exactly when height[i-1] is strictly above threshold.
The scan checks every eligible index once and preserves increasing return order.
editorial: The scan checks every eligible index once and preserves increasing return order.
